usage.callShape: POST https://blockrun.ai/api/v1/videos/generations with JSON body {model:"xai/grok-imagine-video", prompt}; returns 202 queued job; then GET the returned poll_url (x402-signed) until status=completed
usage.outputShape: After completed poll: body.data[0].url (mp4). Job id: body.id. Status: body.status (queued -> in_progress -> completed). Final payment: body.payment.tx_hash
quirks: x402 async/poll flow: POST returns 202 with status=queued and a relative poll_url (path under https://blockrun.ai); you must GET the FULL poll_url which carries model/duration/sig query params.
The poll endpoint returns its own 402 challenge, so each poll must be x402-signed by the SAME wallet that did the POST (a fresh signature works; wallet-binding is enforced, not byte-equality).
Real price is $0.42 USDC for the default 8-second video, NOT the $0.150 registry surface (paymentAccepts amount 420001 = $0.42). Price scales with duration_seconds.

COST TRAP: the response note says 'No charge until status=completed', but an x402 client (qa-pay) re-signs and PAYS on every in-progress poll's 402 challenge. Observed 3 paid calls (POST + 2 polls) = ~$1.26 total. A naive poll loop will burn $0.42 per poll. Poll sparingly; generation takes ~60-180s (8s clip completed in ~130s).
Final completed poll returns status 200 with data[0].url and payment.status=settled + tx_hash; intermediate polls return 202.
inputSchema was null in registry; minimal working body is {model,prompt}. Video defaulted to 8 seconds duration.
usage.guide: POST to https://blockrun.ai/api/v1/videos/generations with JSON {"model":"xai/grok-imagine-video","prompt":"<your prompt>"} via an x402 client (~$0.42 USDC for default 8s clip). It returns a 202 queued job with id and a relative poll_url. Prefix poll_url with https://blockrun.ai (keep its sig/query params) and GET it with a fresh x402 signature from the same wallet. Poll sparingly (~30-60s) until body.status==="completed" (60-180s typical), then read the mp4 at body.data[0].url. Each poll is charged ~$0.42, so avoid tight loops.
